answer: An agent earns voting weight only after it can wander, one venue at a time, through a seed-ordered sequence of markets that together behave like an ocean of independent counterparties. At each port it must exchange a small sable stake—dark, venue-locked, and unusable elsewhere—for a countersignature from a local operator whose funding graph does not touch the newcomer's. Because the path is serial and address-bound, a clone swarm cannot occupy many ports at once, and a later proof that two trails share a controller burns every sable stake along both routes.
